page: Microsoft Azure D16as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 family, powered by AMD EPYC 7763 processors running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an x86_64 architecture with 32 MB L3 cache, standard AVX support, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance alongside steady multi-core execution. The AMD EPYC processor achieved a stress-ng single-core result of 2702.48, placing in the top 25 percent of instances. Multi-core performance is balanced, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9646.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 21578.22. In memory testing, cached 16 KB read throughput measured 1037.17 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB write throughput measured 22.9 GB/sec, representing a lower tier for high-volume memory writes.

With balanced CPU and memory allocation, the instance delivers dependable cost efficiency for general enterprise hosting without the premium overhead of specialized accelerators. Workload testing shows sustained throughput of 17.49 GB/sec for static web serving, 16.0 million Redis SET operations per second, and 312.53 tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter LLM text generation. The configuration is best aligned with multi-tier web applications, intermediate relational database servers, enterprise microservices, and continuous integration pipelines.
